basis: Tumor predisposition alone establishes no affected organ; pulmonary, thyroid and renal lesions require separate diagnoses.

decisions.pulmonary: none: susceptibility to pulmonary tumors or cysts does not establish an existing pulmonary lesion.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: thyroid nodules and neoplasia are separately diagnosed manifestations; predisposition alone establishes no endocrine damage.

basis: Osteochondrodysplasia defines the syndrome. Horseshoe kidney occurs in 30-79%, but fusion alone does not establish renal damage or dysfunction.

decisions.renal: none: horseshoe kidney is frequent (30-79%), but the supplied evidence establishes an anatomical variant without functional injury.

basis: An inherited extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism disorder causes arterial calcification and stenosis. Rickets is occasional (5-29%); renal artery stenosis is cardiovascular.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: deficient extracellular pyrophosphate metabolism is the established disease mechanism, supporting an inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Lysosomal glycogen storage causes skeletal myopathy in most (>80%). Cardiomyopathy is concentrated in infantile Pompe and Danon; its frequency across the umbrella is uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy is subtype-dependent; involvement in at least 30% across the entire umbrella is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: direct storage-associated skeletal myopathy affects most (>80%); the umbrella is defined by lysosomal glycogen storage.

basis: Tooth-forming tissues establish the gastrointestinal origin; the definition also explicitly identifies the jaw skeleton as a primary tumor site.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the maxillofacial skeleton is an explicitly defined site of these tumors, with direct intraosseous occupation.

basis: Congenital spinal cord and column malformation with defining orthopedic changes; persistent neurogenic bladder dysfunction occurs in roughly 30-60%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: spinal-column malformation and skeletal deformities are explicitly part of the disease definition.

basis: Defined by a glycosylation defect, neuromuscular transmission failure and tubular-aggregate muscle pathology. Retinoschisis is reported in 2/4 patients (50%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tubular-aggregate muscle pathology is part of the named disease and parent concept, beyond weakness from junction dysfunction.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; strabismus and ptosis occur in 30-79%. Dental crowding and minor ear/digital morphology do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental anomalies and crowding occur in 30-79%, but impaired dentition or other direct functional injury is not established.

basis: Autoinflammatory sterile abscesses directly affect the spleen in about 70%; liver abscesses occur in 30-79% per HPO. Associated inflammatory bowel disease is separate.

decisions.haematologic: involved: splenic sterile abscesses directly occupy and damage the spleen in about 70%; this is a systemic autoinflammatory syndrome.

basis: Developmental and cardiac defects define syndrome; hearing impairment 4/5, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism 3/4 assessed. Ocular abnormalities and cervical fusion (2/5) omitted at cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: ocular abnormalities are common, but damaging findings lack frequencies; quantified hearing and endocrine dysfunction take priority.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 3/4 assessed; even with male limitation, this supports roughly 30-40% overall involvement.
